ev.q: the percentage of adults aged ≥65 years who had ever received a pneumonia vaccine increased
The percentage increased from 48.0% to 64.8% among adults aged 65–74 years
from 56.4% to 76.3% among adults aged ≥85 years
adults aged 65–74 years were less likely to have ever received a pneumonia vaccine than adults aged ≥75 years
Estimates are based on household interviews of a sample of the civilian, noninstitutionalized U.S. population
During 2000–2018, the percentage of adults aged ≥65 years who had ever received a pneumonia vaccine increased

methods_quotes.q: Unknowns for vaccination status were not included in the denominators when calculating percentages.
